questions.question: State the accounting equation and explain why it always balances. Calculate owner's equity when assets are R250 000 and liabilities R70 000.
questions.expected_answer: A = OE + L. Every asset was supplied either by the owner (owner's equity: capital and retained profits) or by outsiders (liabilities: loans and credit), so total assets must equal the total claims on them. OE = A − L = 250 000 − 70 000 = R180 000.

questions.question: Show the effect on A, OE and L of: (a) owner contributes R80 000 capital; (b) loan of R40 000 received; (c) vehicle bought for R100 000 by EFT; (d) fees of R12 000 received; (e) wages of R4 000 paid; (f) drawings of R2 000; (g) R5 000 of the loan repaid.

Owner's equity was R100 000 at the start of the year and R130 000 at the end. Additional capital of R10 000 was contributed and drawings were R18 000. Calculate the profit and explain three common errors in analysing transactions.
questions.expected_answer: Closing OE = opening OE + capital + profit − drawings: 130 000 = 100 000 + 10 000 + profit − 18 000, so profit = 130 000 − 100 000 − 10 000 + 18 000 = R38 000. Errors: treating a loan received as income (it increases liabilities); treating the purchase of an asset as an expense (it exchanges one asset for another, OE unchanged); treating drawings as an expense (drawings reduce OE but not profit).
